01Dataset scope and grower locations

Four growers, ten fields each, five crop years of CDL/MNC, and 1,826 daily weather records per farm.

The runtime covers two US regions and one Argentine province: Illinois and Iowa are the corn–soy core, Nebraska is drier and corn-heavy, and Entre Ríos is a southern-hemisphere soy/pasture system. Locations are the mean field centroid per grower.

Weather is the exception that proves the rule: 40 fields resolve to 10 distinct daily series (AR 1, NE 2, IA 3, IL 4), so the honest weather unit is the series, not the field.

Two statistical views and one comparison/correlation analysis.

Kruskal–WallisCompactness, 4 growersε² = 0.52< 0.001

Mann–Whitney + HolmArea, AR vs ILCliff's δ = -1.000.001

Argentina is a separate field-size population (Cliff's δ = −1.00 against every US grower), while Iowa and Illinois are statistically indistinguishable in area (δ = +0.02). The size–shape correlation is real across the pooled set but vanishes within each grower, which is the honest reading: the trend is driven by AR's small, blocky parcels versus IL's large, elongated ones.

05CDL / cropland

Two statistical views and one comparison analysis over 200 field-years.

Comparison — cropland/crop_tests.csv

ComparisonEffect sizepNote
grower x dominant crop (all field-years)Cramér's V = 0.49< 0.001expected counts adequate
grower x crop-change (consecutive years)Cramér's V = 0.59< 0.001expected counts adequate
IL rotation descriptor90 % of year pairs change · 2.0 effective crops—descriptive
IA rotation descriptor97.5 % of year pairs change · 2.0 effective crops—descriptive
NE rotation descriptor32.5 % of year pairs change · 1.6 effective crops—descriptive
AR rotation descriptor45 % of year pairs change · 2.8 effective crops—descriptive

Crop mix and rotation rigidity are both grower-specific: chi-square V = 0.49 for the dominant-class mix and 0.59 for whether the class changes between consecutive years, with adequate expected counts (minimum 5.75). Iowa and Illinois are strict corn–soy alternators; Nebraska is corn-heavy with two rotating parcels; Argentina is a mixed pasture/soy system with ten split field-years.

Correlation and independence — weather/weather_series_correlation.csv

45 pairwise daily correlations over 1,826 days. Within a grower, series are near-duplicates (r(T2M) ≥ 0.998, r(precip) 0.88–0.95), so fields inside one grower are not independent climate replicates. Argentina versus the US runs at r(T2M) ≈ -0.77 — the expected southern-hemisphere inversion, not an error.

What is null by construction. Argentina has one weather series for all ten fields, so a within-grower weather comparison there has no replication. The audit table states this rather than reporting noise.

07Geospatial maps

Three static plates: layout, latest crop class, and the weather grid. Grower-local metre axes, boxed north arrow, Esri World Imagery underlay, no scale bar.

08Limitations, missing data, and assumptions

  • Boundaries are one snapshot. There is no boundary-change history; only cropland and weather carry time.
  • Weather repeats per field. 40 field rows collapse to 10 daily series; summing raw rows would inflate annual precipitation and GDD ten-fold, so every aggregate de-duplicates first.
  • Argentina has a single series, so its within-grower weather spread is climate, not field variation.
  • No yield, imagery indices, or soil are used. This is a land-cover, geometry, and climate comparison only.
  • p-values are descriptive at n = 4 growers. Ten fields are not ten independent climate observations, and the growers were not sampled; effect sizes carry the claim.
  • Split threshold is 60 %. A field-year is split when the dominant class holds less than 60 % of the pixels, so a field-year label can hide a real mixture.
  • Maps are county scale. Individual parcels are 1–3 % of panel width and carry no per-field id; ids and measurements live in the CSVs.
  • Crop class is table-derived. The boundary crop hint is a human/OSM override slot and is never used as evidence.

09Soil

Soil analysis was not required and is not the focus of this work. No soil layer, SSURGO/gNATSGO product, or soil-texture analysis is read, plotted, or reported here. The three categories are field boundaries, CDL/cropland, and weather.
